- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or shows strong downward momentum, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk-off bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — cap forecast peak at 1.5–2x recent high.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is > 20% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., 1.0 → 0.0), model often fails to adjust — force a downward correction in next 5–7 days.
- Forecast bias is more pronounced in early horizon (1–7 days) — model tends to overreact to sentiment; use sentiment-weighted smoothing for first 7 days.
